comparison: Both strongly support the technical methodology claims (C8, C102-C106). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation and minimal phototoxicity, while peer reviewers praised it as a 'technical tour de force' enabling longitudinal tracking impossible with head-fixed imaging. Complete agreement on technical achievement.

Both support state-dependent morphological changes (C29-C33). OpenEval highlights converging quantitative evidence from 2D/3D imaging with adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers affirmed 'solid evidence' for brain-state-dependent regulation and noted differential NREM/REM responses. Both evaluate C9 and C66 as well-supported main conclusions.

Both support the distinction between anesthesia and natural sleep (C38-C39). OpenEval notes quantitative differential responses but suggests more characterization needed. Peer reviewers explicitly highlighted this as a 'key advance' for understanding microglia in naturalistic conditions versus anesthesia.

Both support sleep deprivation-induced morphological changes (C41-C47, C85). OpenEval emphasizes time-course data showing early onset at 3 hours contradicting prior studies, with quantitative measurements and reversibility. Peer reviewers affirmed 'important evidence' and specifically noted the novel early timing finding.

Both address recovery findings (C40, C45). OpenEval includes these in broader sleep deprivation evaluation as demonstrating reversibility. Peer reviewers accepted recovery findings as supporting dynamic and reversible nature of microglial responses without concerns.

Both support state-dependent norepinephrine fluctuations (C48-C51, C53). OpenEval notes GRABNE2m biosensor measurements with statistical significance and considers C54 a reasonable inference requiring further validation. Peer reviewers accepted NE findings as providing 'important evidence' for NE as modulator, evaluating C11 as well-supported.

Both support LC-NE necessity via DSP4 experiments (C57-C59). OpenEval finds 'compelling evidence' from complete abolishment of state-dependent and SD-induced changes with validated LC ablation. Peer reviewers affirmed findings, noting agreement with previous publications and highlighting 'critical role of norepinephrine.'

Both address β2AR knockout findings (C61-C65, C69) but differ in confidence. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while acknowledging pan-tissue KO limitation (C94). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing 'significant reservations' that data 'cannot be used to state a direct effect on microglia dynamics' and emphasizing need for microglia-specific studies.

Both support main conclusions synthesizing findings (C9, C66-C69). OpenEval emphasizes convergence of imaging, biosensor, and genetic/pharmacological data. Peer reviewers affirmed 'main conclusions are well validated and supported,' noting solid evidence for brain-state-dependent regulation.

Partial overlap on LC-NE mechanism conclusions (C12, C68). OpenEval groups these with broader conclusions as well-supported by multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers specifically affirmed LC-NE dependency findings as providing important evidence.

Both address functional implications (C74, C78). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting morphological observations are solid but functional implications (enhanced clearance, memory consolidation) are speculative without direct measurements. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting interpretations as logical extensions consistent with cited literature.

Partial overlap on morphology-function relationship (C34, C36). OpenEval includes these in state-dependent morphology evaluation, considering C36 a reasonable inference from C35. Peer reviewers accepted functional interpretations without critique as logical extensions of morphological findings.

Both support baseline characterization claims (C24-C27). OpenEval includes these in technical validation showing quantitative measurements. Peer reviewers accepted baseline findings without critique, praising longitudinal tracking capability that enabled these observations.

OpenEval rates literature discrepancy explanations (C75-C77, C82-C84, C86) as UNCERTAIN, noting proposed explanations for contradictions with prior studies are plausible but speculative and not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates background literature citations (C88-C93) as SUPPORTED for establishing biological plausibility of LC-NE-β2AR mechanism, noting these are contextual claims rather than novel findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates alternative mechanism proposals (C95-C98) as UNCERTAIN, noting cited evidence is valid but actual contribution to microglial regulation is speculative and untested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C7, C14-C23, C35, C70-C71, C73, C79-C80) as SUPPORTED, noting these are appropriately cited contextual claims from established literature rather than novel findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates limitation acknowledgments (C52, C81, C94, C99, C101) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate scientific rigor in acknowledging unknowns, particularly pan-tissue β2AR KO limitation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
